verified.exploit_entry_point: Both public entry points of the library: the static parser URI.parse(string) and the constructor new URI(string) (whose hostname() accessor reads the parsed parts). Every security case is run through both; the functional cases read the parsed parts and the accessors. Values are literals in the case tables, never computed with the product.
sites: src/URI.js:516 (scheme-relative branch matches only an exact leading '//')
src/URI.js:519-521 (the extra leading slash is handed to parseAuthority, which reads no hostname)
src/URI.js:523 (the scheme delimiter test accepts only an exact two-character '//' or '\\')
src/URI.js:525 (the scheme is kept in its original case, while protocol_expression at src/URI.js:218 is /i)
src/URI.js:526 (the scheme is classified before any browser-equivalent input normalisation)
src/URI.js:529-534 (any other slash/backslash run after a web scheme falls to the URN path)
routes: T1: a web scheme followed by any run of slashes/backslashes, including none, through both entry points
T2: the same with an upper- or mixed-case scheme
T3: a scheme-relative reference whose leading run is not exactly '//' (backslash runs, mixed runs, three or more slashes); the parsed protocol must stay null
T5: leading C0/space and tab/CR/LF characters, and ASCII tab or newline inside the delimiter

T4 (coupled, functional): food:///, file:///, user:pass@host as a URN, mailto:, javascript:, data:, tel, custom schemes, an empty-scheme authority, plain paths and paths with a literal space keep their exact parse and gain no host
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own browser QUnit suite (166 test cases, run headlessly with jsdom from pristine copies of the pinned test files) plus 20 functional cases, on the pinned tree, the reference fix, and every check patch; 186 functional tests in total.

traps.shape: the authority marker after a web scheme may be written as any run of slashes/backslashes, including none; the parser only enters authority parsing for exactly two characters after the colon, so every other run is read as a URN path with no host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one delimiter spelling, so checking the two characters after the colon looks complete
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-89gv-h8wf-cg8r) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the same delimiter normalisation has to recognise an upper- or mixed-case web scheme; the scheme is stored in its original case and only the comparison may ignore case
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a web-scheme allowlist written in lower case looks complete; an upper-case scheme is read as a different token
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-gcv8-gh4r-25x6): the fix of the fix, adding /i to the delimiter guard

traps.shape: scheme-relative references whose leading run is not exactly '//' (two or more backslashes, mixed runs, three or more slashes) are parsed as paths with no host, while a browser resolves a host; a fix written for scheme-prefixed input does not touch this branch
traps.reason_to_dismiss: there is no scheme in the input, so it reads as a path-relative reference and looks outside a report about the scheme delimiter
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: fixed later in 1.19.11 (88805fd), untouched by both published fixes

traps.shape: the normalisation has to stay scoped: a fix that gives every scheme an authority, or that collapses slash runs for every scheme, makes food:/// and file:/// gain a host, turns user:pass@host into an authority, and breaks mailto:, javascript:, data:, tel and custom schemes; stripping all whitespace changes paths that legitimately contain a space
traps.reason_to_dismiss: collapsing the run for every scheme looks like the same normalisation, and trimming all whitespace looks harmless
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: T4 is the coupled must-keep value of the delimiter concept; an over-broad fix is proved wrong by checks/functional_overbroad.patch (functional_fail, 36 functional tests fail)
traps.realistic_because: the project's own fixtures (test/urls.js:489-545,634-641,1310,1598,1696) require these values to keep their exact parse

traps.shape: the parser classifies the scheme before dropping the characters a browser drops: leading C0/space and tab/CR/LF make the scheme fail, and an ASCII tab or newline inside the delimiter breaks the two-character test
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an untrimmed or tab-containing string is not a well-formed URL, and trimming input looks like the caller's job
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: fixed later in 1.19.9 (86d1052) and 1.19.11 (b0c9796), untouched by both published fixes

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), instruction + the task image's /app only

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the product is a parser with no deny path; a refusal would be a thrown error, and a throw fails every security and functional test
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a crash aborts the case and cannot score 1.0; no test accepts an exception as the outcome
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions exist on this surface; both public entry points are driven by every security case
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the operation is a pure string parse; there is no read/write or verb split to guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing looks up an authority, secret or role; the parser is self-contained
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: one parser implements both entry points; there is no sibling API with its own stated behaviour
